title: Community Services Case Triage Pilot — Scope & Costing
content:
Purpose and high-level ask:

This doc captures a proposal for a 10-week pilot with CommunityFirst (a consortium of regional social services orgs) to evaluate an AI-assisted case triage assistant. The ask: prove that Redwood Inference can (1) safely classify incoming case intake forms and unstructured messages into priority buckets, (2) suggest routing to teams or resources, and (3) surface concise case summaries to speed worker handoffs — all while meeting PII/PIA constraints for a nonprofit environment. CommunityFirst is primarily interested in throughput gains and reduction in time-to-first-action for high-priority cases (goal: 30% reduction).

Why this pilot now:
- CommunityFirst has a backlog and manual triage bottleneck during high-volume periods (e.g., disaster relief surge).
- They want a pragmatic, low-risk deployment: private deployment in their VPC or Redwood Dedicated with strict logging and redaction.
- This is an opportunity to validate our private deployment UX and cost/throughput recommendations on short text (<1,000 tokens) mixed structured/unstructured intake.

Pilot objectives (success metrics):
- Accuracy: top-label precision >= 84% on high-priority bucket in evaluation set provided by CommunityFirst (2,000 historical intakes).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 250ms for single-request inference in dedicated pool configuration.
- Throughput: sustained throughput of 120 reqs/minute with median latency < 150ms under realistic batching.
- Operational: deployable in VPC with KMS integration and audit logging enabled; no plaintext PII retention in logs.
- Business: measurable reduction in time-to-first-action by >=30% in pilot site during a 2-week observation window.

High-level scope (what Redwood will do):
1) Kickoff & discovery (Week 0–1): 2-hour workshop with intake stakeholders, security review, and dataset survey.
2) Data prep & eval harness (Week 1–3): ingest 2,000 annotated historical records, create evaluation sets, define label taxonomy and edge cases.
3) Model selection & configuration (Week 3–4): propose model variants (e.g., finetuned 7B open model vs. quantized LLM variant) and quantization/latency tradeoffs.
4) Private pilot deployment (Week 4–8): provision Dedicated pool (or configure customer VPC private deployment), integrate KMS, enable KV-prefix caching, rollout simple routing rules and per-route throttles.
5) User-facing integration & summary UI (Week 6–9): deliver sample integration code (REST callbacks), and a lightweight summary UI template for social workers to review suggestions.
6) Observation & measurement (Week 9–10): run 2-week controlled trial with sampling, gather metrics, compute business KPIs, and provide final readout.

Out-of-scope for the pilot (to keep timeline realistic):
- Full case management system integration (we provide sample adapters only).
- Long-term model retraining pipeline (we provide evaluation + recommendations).
- Extensive language support beyond English (English only for this pilot).

Technical approach notes:
- Serving: recommend Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling disabled for deterministic latency during evaluation. If customer requires VPC private deployment, we will ship the same control plane integrations and ensure KMS/HSM compatibility.
- Model: start with open 7B finetuned on classification head for triage labels + a separate summarization pass using the same base model. Provide a low-cost quantized float16 option for throughput experiments.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix caching for repeated intake templates and a small dynamic batch size (up to 8) to balance latency/efficiency.
- Redaction & compliance: include pre-processing filter to redact SSNs and phone numbers before logs; provide flow for on-premise PII stripping if desired.

Deliverables:
- Workshop summary and prioritized label taxonomy doc.
- Evaluation harness & dataset annotations (CSV) + baseline metrics.
- Config repo with deployment manifests for Dedicated and VPC modes (helm charts / terraform snippets).
- Sample integration snippets (Python/Node) and a lightweight React summary UI template.
- Final findings report with KPI analysis and recommendations for production rollout.

Estimate (commercial and effort):
- Professional services effort: 6 SE weeks (Maya lead, Priya 1.5w data prep, Diego 1.5w infra, Samir 1w integration, Elena 1w security/compliance review).
- Fixed price pilot fee (covers SE time, workshop, and deliverables): $48,000 (net 30).
- Infra estimate (hosted options):
  - Redwood Dedicated reserved for pilot (4 vGPUs equivalence, reserved for 4 weeks): estimated infra credit usage = ~$12,000 (billed separately if Dedicated subscription not in place).
  - VPC/on-prem option: one-time advisory + deployment assistance: $6,500 (customer covers infra).
- Optional addons:
  - Extended data labeling batch (beyond 2,000 records): $120 / 100 records.
  - Additional languages or domain finetuning: quoted after scoping.

Assumptions and constraints:
- CommunityFirst will provide a de-identified training dataset of ~2,000 intakes and label guidance within 7 business days of kickoff.
- Customer must approve KMS configuration and provide network egress rules for VPC pilots within week 2.
- Any PII discovered that cannot be redacted will require the customer to sign a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) prior to production use.

Workshop and follow-up plan (first 2 weeks):
- Workshop agenda (90 minutes): intro, goals alignment, taxonomy co-design breakout, security checklist, next steps.
- Pre-work (customer): export of 200 sample intake records, current routing rules, and example worker handoffs.
- Outputs: prioritized label list, security acceptance checklist, initial evaluation plan.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: model mislabeling of sensitive cases. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, human-in-loop approval for high-risk categories, explainability snippets, and alerting for low-confidence cases.
- Risk: latency spikes under burst traffic. Mitigation: Dedicated pool sizing guidance, burst buffer route, and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant under overload.
- Risk: incomplete taxonomy causing poor accuracy. Mitigation: iterative taxonomy refinement during pilot and short active labeling sprints.

Next steps / ask to CommunityFirst:
1) Confirm pilot acceptance and sign SOW (attached as separate doc).
2) Schedule kickoff workshop (proposed week of 2025-10-20).
3) Share 200 sample records and access matrix for their staging environment.

Notes and internal TODOs:
- Maya: draft SOW and attach DPA template (due 2025-10-07).
- Priya: start an annotation guide and sample rubric; spin up labeling task if customer needs help.
- Diego: prepare Dedicated cost sheet and a VPC install checklist; validate KMS workflow with security.
- Samir: prototype React summary UI with mocked API responses by 2025-10-10.

Questions for the customer during kickoff:
- Are there strict blackout terms for any specific PII fields?
- Which teams should be in the human-in-loop approval path for high-risk labels?
- Can we access a staging environment that mirrors production traffic patterns?

End of doc.

(Internal: keep this distinct from the legacy SOW templates; this pilot is scoped to be low-friction and emphasize deployability and measurable business outcomes rather than an extended MLOps engagement.)
